79596.body:
The Economist Picks

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/what-worlds-loveliest-language-the-economist-t0aee?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3Bc6BeYJsuT%2Fm4BilQxBF8Rg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=30MsvDN8UlgYs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mue0coj4~tu-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mue0coj4-tu
  
Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our senior editors. Most people have a vague sense that some languages just seem prettier than others. And if you are a language-learner, maybe there are ones you just enjoy speaking more than others. (I freely confess a soft spot for Brazilian Portuguese.) You might think your views would be widely shared by any observer. You might be surprised. This proposition has been tested by a group of researchers who played identical texts in dozens of languages to speakers who themselves spoke several different languages. The conclusion: a universal linguistic beauty queen is hard to find. Most languages were rated pretty similarly—and the one that won the highest rating is probably not one you would guess.
